topic: JavaScript basics: functions, strings and validation
title: Validate a sign-up form with JavaScript
instructions:
## Check before you send

A sign-up form on a Ghanaian site collects an email, a password and a phone number. Write the validation functions the page will call before submitting.

1. `isValidEmail(text)`: true when there is exactly one `@`, at least one character before it, and a dot somewhere after it (not immediately after the `@`).
2. `passwordStrength(pw)`: `"weak"` under 8 characters; `"medium"` when 8 or more with letters only or digits only; `"strong"` when 8 or more with both letters and digits.
3. `formatPhone(text)`: accept `0241234567` or `+233241234567` (spaces allowed) and return `+233 24 123 4567`; return `null` for anything else.
hints: text.indexOf("@") and text.lastIndexOf("@") must be equal and greater than 0; the dot must be after the @ plus one.
Remove spaces, turn a leading 0 into +233, then check it is +233 followed by 9 digits before slicing it into groups.
realityNote: Browser validation is for the user's convenience; the server must validate again because anyone can bypass the page. HTML5 input types (email, tel) and the pattern attribute give you a first layer for free.
